1. source.py generates a 1024-bit RSA key, encrypts the flag with PKCS1_OAEP (default SHA-1/MGF1-SHA1) and writes n, ct, plus partial leaks of the primes: p = str(key.p)[::2] (every 2nd decimal digit starting at index 0) and q = str(key.q)[1::2] (every 2nd digit starting at index 1).
2. Leak lengths (78 digits for p, 77 for q) plus n's 309 digits pin both primes at 155 decimal digits. Counting digit positions from the least-significant end, p is known at even offsets and q at odd offsets (offset 154 for both since 155 is odd), so at every position exactly one digit is known and the other is the only unknown.
3. solve.py performs a least-significant-digit-first DFS, extending partial low halves (p_low, q_low) with the forced/leaked digit on one side and 0–9 on the other, pruning unless p_low*q_low ≡ n (mod 10^(k+1)), forbidding leading zeros. Exactly one candidate survives in 101 ms.
